mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and retail sales signals a strengthening demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint correlation between HOUST and RSAFS increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as immediate concerns about economic health arise.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between PAYEMS decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPI) over two consecutive months signals inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded and monetary policy tightening becomes more likely.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real GDP and retail sales signals a broad-based weakening of demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity and corporate earnings expectations decline.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both decrease > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint correlation between GDPC1 and RSAFS decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
